rules: Consumption is an atomic durable transaction completed before the first target database connection.
Consumed authority is never restored, including after process crash.
Every retry requires a new exact approval and attempt ID.
Duplicate approvals, payloads, attempts and terminal events are rejected.
Expired, partial, malformed, mutated or mismatched approvals are rejected before connection.
Every consumed attempt must reconcile to exactly one terminal state.
A missing terminal event remains detectable as an incomplete consumed attempt.
Terminal failure or abort creates no further access authority.

failure_recovery.before_consumption: Fail without authority consumption and create a sanitized rejection record; no target connection.
failure_recovery.after_consumption_before_connection: Record or reconcile an incomplete consumed attempt to AUDIT_ABORTED; never restore or retry authority.
failure_recovery.after_connection: Close connection on every path, finalize bounded sanitized evidence if safe, and record exactly one terminal state.
failure_recovery.partial_artifacts: Keep in task-scoped temporary storage, mark noncanonical, and never replace an existing finalized attempt.
failure_recovery.missing_terminal: Reconciliation reports INCOMPLETE_CONSUMED_ATTEMPT and blocks all reuse or promotion.
